nutshell: Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) can generate a referring expression for an object (REG) and separately localize an object from an expression (REC), but the two capabilities are trained independently and are often inconsistent with each other - especially on out-of-domain images. SC-Tune fine-tunes a 'describer' and a 'locator' (two roles played by the same LVLM) in an alternating cycle where each supplies the training signal for the other via a bbox-to-caption-to-bbox round trip, improving both REC and REG jointly without needing any human-written referring-expression annotations.
contributions: Defines 'self-consistency' (the bbox->caption->bbox round-trip) as an explicit reliability metric for LVLM referential comprehension and shows it drops sharply on out-of-domain images for two existing LVLMs (Table 1, e.g. Qwen-VL 87.9 in-domain vs. 52.9 on OpenImages).

SC-Tune training paradigm: alternates PPO-based RL fine-tuning of the 'describer' (rewarded by IoU between the original bbox and the locator's reconstruction of it from the describer's generated caption, with a token-level KL penalty and a value-free 'REINFORCE with baseline' advantage instead of a separate learned value network) with supervised MLE fine-tuning of the 'locator' on the describer's own self-generated captions, synchronizing parameters between the two roles after each phase.

Fully data-efficient in terms of human annotation: needs only ~166K images + bounding boxes (Object365) and zero text annotations, since the captions used to train the locator are entirely self-generated by the describer.

Shows consistent gains across two different LVLM backbones (Qwen-VL, MiniGPT-v2) on out-of-domain REC/REG (ReferItGame, Flickr30K) and referential QA (Visual-7W, Local-QA), while image-level benchmarks (Nocaps, Flickr30K captioning, VQAv2, GQA) hold steady or improve slightly.
deficiencies: In-domain REC performance (RefCOCO, Table 3) actually drops after SC-Tune for both backbones on val/testA (Qwen-VL: 88.88->88.04, 92.27->90.77; MiniGPT-v2: 84.84->83.59, 89.49->88.50). The paper's explanation - that the generated caption style 'gradually deviates from the in-domain style' - is asserted with no direct measurement of that drift, and the proposed fix (mixing in supervised RefCOCO data during locator training) is framed as an afterthought 'attempt' rather than integrated into the main method or ablated cleanly.

The 'comparable with the fully supervised model' zero-shot claim (Table 2, vs. CLIP-VG) glosses over the fact that SC-Tune is fine-tuned directly on bbox/image pairs from a large detection dataset (Object365) that is structurally very close to the grounding task itself - it isn't zero-shot in the sense of never having seen bbox-localization training signal, only in the sense of never seeing the target REC/REG datasets' own annotations, which the paper doesn't distinguish explicitly.

The Value-Free Advantage (Eq. 3) - replacing a learned PPO value function with a single greedily-decoded baseline caption per sample - is presented as a design contribution, but there's no ablation isolating whether this simplification costs any performance relative to a standard PPO setup with a real value network.

The method requires substantial extra machinery versus a plain supervised baseline (PPO reinforcement learning, reward shaping with a KL coefficient, alternating freeze/train cycles, 8xA100 for 10-15 hours per model), but Table 8's ablation only compares isolated-component tuning (locator-only vs. describer-only vs. both) - it never compares against a simpler 'just jointly supervised fine-tune on REC+REG' baseline without the RL cycle, so it's unclear how much of the gain specifically requires the RL self-consistency loop versus ordinary multi-task fine-tuning.
notable: The locator is trained purely on the describer's own self-generated (not ground-truth) captions via ordinary supervised MLE - so the entire pipeline bootstraps referential comprehension from bare bbox coordinates with zero human-written referring expressions at any point, a 'self-play'-style pattern that could generalize to other cyclic-consistency tasks beyond visual grounding. Also worth flagging: despite matching this literature review's ReID-related search terms (the abstract uses 're-identify the objects' to describe the REG->REC round trip), this paper is not about person re-identification at all - it's about referring-expression grounding/captioning consistency in general-purpose LVLMs, and 're-identify' here just means 'relocate the same object,' unrelated to person-ReID as a task.
